slot.topic_title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for the Difference Between Two Population Means

item.title: Estimating a Difference in Mean Exam Scores Between Two Schools
item.stimulus: A district compares a common end-of-year exam at two schools. Independent random samples were taken: 32 students from School 1 (mean 78.4, standard deviation 11.2) and 35 students from School 2 (mean 72.1, standard deviation 9.8). Each sample is less than 10% of its school's students.

parts.prompt: Show that the conditions for the appropriate procedure for estimating the difference in mean exam score are met.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two schools.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two schools.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the students at its school.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of the students at its school.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: both sample sizes (32 and 35) are at least 30.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: both sample sizes (32 and 35) are at least 30.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

parts.prompt: Technology gives 95% confidence with approximately 61.9 degrees of freedom, so t* = 1.999. Calculate the standard error and the interval for μ₁ − μ₂.

criteria.text: Calculates the standard error √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂) = √(11.2²/32 + 9.8²/35) = 2.581 points.
criteria.evidence: Response computes the standard error from the sample statistics and reports about 2.581 points.
criteria.fix: Use the standard error formula for this procedure with the sample standard deviation(s) and sample size(s).

criteria.text: Computes the interval (78.4 − 72.1) ± 1.999(2.581) = 1.14 to 11.46 points, using t* = 1.999.
criteria.evidence: Response adds and subtracts t* times the standard error, giving an interval from 1.14 to 11.46 points.
criteria.fix: Add and subtract t* times the standard error from the sample statistic, using the given critical value.

parts.prompt: State the point estimate for μ₁ − μ₂.

criteria.text: States the point estimate for μ₁ − μ₂ as x̄₁ − x̄₂ = 78.4 − 72.1 = 6.3 points.
criteria.evidence: Response states 6.3 points (or an equivalent form) as the point estimate for the difference in means.
criteria.fix: Estimate a difference in population means with the difference in sample means, subtracting in the order the parameter is written.

item.model_answer:
(a) The procedure is a two-sample t-interval for a difference in population means. Randomization: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two schools. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the students at its school. Sample-data condition: both sample sizes (32 and 35) are at least 30.

(b) SE = √(11.2²/32 + 9.8²/35) = 2.581 points. The interval is (78.4 − 72.1) ± 1.999(2.581) = 1.14 to 11.46 points.

(c) The point estimate is x̄₁ − x̄₂ = 78.4 − 72.1 = 6.3 points.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure for estimating the difference in mean exam score and show that its conditions are met.
